title: Reverse map after twice the annihilating line twist
statement:
Let $Z$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $s:\mathcal L\to\mathcal O_Z$ a module morphism, and $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H(r)=\mathcal H\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes r}$ for $r\in\mathbf Z$, using dual tensor powers for negative $r$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $\delta_e:\mathcal H(r)\to\mathcal H(r-e)$ be induced by $s^{\otimes e}$ for $e\geq0$. Let $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose the maps $\delta_c:(\ker\alpha)(c)\to\ker\alpha$ and $\delta_c:(\operatorname{coker}\alpha)(c)\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ are zero. There exists a morphism $\beta:\mathcal G(2c)\to\mathcal F$ such that
$$\alpha\circ\beta=\delta_{2c}:\mathcal G(2c)\to\mathcal G,\qquad \beta\circ\alpha(2c)=\delta_{2c}:\mathcal F(2c)\to\mathcal F.$$
In particular, for every integer $r$, twisting $\beta$ gives $\beta_r:\mathcal G(r)\to\mathcal F(r-2c)$ with $\alpha(r-2c)\circ\beta_r=\delta_{2c}$. No regularity of $s$ and no finiteness of the sheaves is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a Zariski cover trivializing $\mathcal L$. On a trivializing open $U$ choose a frame $e$, put $a=s(e)$, and identify twists with the original sheaves using $e^{\otimes r}$ (the dual frame for $r<0$). The tensor definition gives $\delta_c(h\otimes e^{\otimes c})=a^ch$. Thus $a^c$ kills every section of $\ker\alpha$ and of $\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ on every open in $U$. Let $q:\mathcal G\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ be the sheafified sectionwise quotient, as in the module-category description.

source.place: Tag 0GAC, lemma-factor-hom, proof: the small detail omitted in the factorization through the dual comparison; local lift construction supplied by Q11.

proof.text: For an open $V\subseteq U$ and $g\in\mathcal G(V)$, linearity gives $q(a^cg)=a^cq(g)=0$. Apply the local-image statement to the ringed space $(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$, the morphism $\alpha$, and its canonical sheafified quotient $q$: there is an open cover $V_i$ of $V$ with $x_i\in\mathcal F(V_i)$ and $\alpha(x_i)=a^cg|_{V_i}$. This uses local lifts only, not surjectivity on sections.

source.place: Tag 0GAC, lemma-factor-hom, proof: the small detail omitted in the factorization through the dual comparison; local lift construction supplied by Q11.

proof.text: On $V_i\cap V_j$, the difference $x_i-x_j$ lies in the sectionwise kernel, so $a^c(x_i-x_j)=0$. The sheaf axiom glues the $a^cx_i$ to a section $b_e(g)\in\mathcal F(V)$. A second family of lifts gives the same section, by the same difference calculation on intersections. Restricting the lifts proves compatibility with restriction. For $g+h$ and $tg$, use the lifts $x_i+y_j$ on a common refinement and $tx_i$, respectively; uniqueness of gluing gives $b_e(g+h)=b_e(g)+b_e(h)$ and $b_e(tg)=tb_e(g)$. Thus $b_e:\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal F|_U$ is a module-sheaf morphism.

source.place: Tag 0GAC, lemma-factor-hom, proof: the small detail omitted in the factorization through the dual comparison; local lift construction supplied by Q11.

proof.text: For another frame $e'=ue$ on an overlap, where $u$ is a unit, one has $a'=ua$. If $\alpha(x)=a^cg$ locally, then $u^cx$ lifts $(a')^cg$, whence $b_{e'}(g)=(a')^cu^cx=u^{2c}b_e(g)$. Therefore the maps defined by $\beta(g\otimes e^{\otimes 2c})=b_e(g)$ agree on overlaps, since $e'^{\otimes 2c}=u^{2c}e^{\otimes 2c}$. Apply the sheaf gluing axiom to their values on each section; equality on overlaps and uniqueness give a global linear morphism $\beta:\mathcal G(2c)\to\mathcal F$ commuting with restrictions.

source.place: Tag 0GAC, lemma-factor-hom, proof: the small detail omitted in the factorization through the dual comparison; local lift construction supplied by Q11.

proof.text: Locally $\alpha(b_e(g))=\alpha(a^cx)=a^{2c}g$, so $\alpha\beta=\delta_{2c}$. For $f\in\mathcal F(V)$, the section $a^cf$ itself is a lift of $a^c\alpha(f)$; hence $b_e(\alpha(f))=a^{2c}f$, giving $\beta\alpha(2c)=\delta_{2c}$. These equalities on the trivializing cover imply the asserted global equalities by separatedness of the sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0GAC, lemma-factor-hom, proof: the small detail omitted in the factorization through the dual comparison; local lift construction supplied by Q11.

proof.text: For $r\in\mathbf Z$, tensor $\beta$ by $\mathcal L^{\otimes(r-2c)}$. The dual frame evaluates to $1$ on $e$, so on each trivializing open the tensor identifications give $\beta_r(g\otimes e^{\otimes r})=b_e(g)\otimes e^{\otimes(r-2c)}$. Applying $\alpha(r-2c)$ gives $a^{2c}g\otimes e^{\otimes(r-2c)}$, exactly $\delta_{2c}$ on that frame. This proves the final clause, including negative $r$, and nowhere cancels $a$ or assumes finite generation.
